{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c59a8d729b9f21f49872b2c83994287180b34dc7d64b0523c73be8d65c9c779d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:60","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle information confusables and continuation details","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: two-year versus annual inspections, five-year versus one-year dealer stickers, and continuation details on ownership proof, plates, specialty inspections and insurance fraud","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: two-year versus annual inspections, five-year versus one-year dealer stickers, and continuation details on ownership proof, plates, specialty inspections and insurance fraud
Confusable pairs among vehicle paperwork rules, followed by continuation facts the C block left out for size; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A03
Passenger vehicles are inspected every two years, but commercial-registered vehicles covered by the rule are inspected every year. [A03]
Why it matters: group inspection; confusable two-year versus annual inspection.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A03
A new passenger vehicle's dealer sticker runs five years, while a commercial-registered vehicle under one year old bought from a dealer gets a sticker that runs one year. [A03]
Why it matters: group inspection; confusable five-year versus one-year sticker.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A03
Diesel passenger vehicles from model year 1997 on, more than five model years old and with a gross vehicle weight rating of 8,500 pounds or less, must pass an emissions inspection every two years. [A03]
Why it matters: group inspection; confusable gasoline versus diesel model years.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A03
A new resident's passenger vehicle under five model years old is exempt from inspection and gets a new car dealer sticker expiring five years from the model year. [A03]
Why it matters: group inspection; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A03
High-rise and reconstructed vehicles must go to one of the MVC Specialty Inspection sites in Eatontown, Secaucus or Winslow. [A03]
Why it matters: group inspection; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A03
Inspections take place at a State inspection station or at a State-licensed private inspection facility (PIF). [A03]
Why it matters: group inspection; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0162]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A01
Only the titled owner, or someone authorized to act for the owner, may process a title and registration transaction at an MVC Vehicle Center. [A01]
Why it matters: group registration; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A01
A leased vehicle needs a power of attorney issued by the leasing company, and for a leased or financed out-of-state vehicle, get the original title from the lien holder or leasing company. [A01]
Why it matters: group registration; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0160]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A02
Most plates can be transferred to your next vehicle, and plates not transferred after a sale must be surrendered to the MVC in person or by mail, keeping the receipt. [A02]
Why it matters: group plates; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A02
Only valid plates may be placed on a vehicle. [A02]
Why it matters: group plates; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0161]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A04
The type and cost of insurance coverage vary, and the Department of Banking and Insurance website lists coverage choices. [A04]
Why it matters: group insurance; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0163]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A04
Insurance fraud through a false claim or application can lead to criminal charges and jail, civil fines of up to $15,000 per violation, and possible loss of the driver license. [A04]
Why it matters: group insurance; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0163]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A04
Fraud raises insurance costs for everyone in New Jersey, and tips to the Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor are kept anonymous and confidential. [A04]
Why it matters: group insurance; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0163]
